title: Supplementary Table S28. Multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis of the primary continuous-exposure models.
notes_after: Note. Multiple imputation by chained equations (20 imputations, 10 iterations, predictive mean matching) was applied to the variables of the primary model; derived variables (log-consumption, climatic principal components) were recomputed within each imputed dataset before fitting the dual-exposure mixed model, and estimates were pooled with Rubin's rules. FMI: fraction of missing information. Relative difference compares the MI-pooled and single-imputation estimates. This analysis addressed only remaining missing values in the supplied dataset and did not recover uncertainty from the earlier deterministic imputation. Models used restricted maximum likelihood and model-based standard errors rather than the primary robust variance estimator. Abbreviations: CI, confidence interval; EVI, enhanced vegetation index; FMI, fraction of missing information; IQR, interquartile range; MI, multiple imputation; O₃, ozone.
